newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European markets rise despite rate prospects.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European markets rise despite rate prospects.

text.p: European stocks and bonds staged a turnaround on Tuesday after investors accepted the idea that U.S. interest rates are set to rise for the first time in more than two years and drove the Dow Jones index strongly higher.
All three of Europe's major bourses -- London, Paris and Frankfurt -- rose in early trading, while the dollar drifted in a very narrow range against the mark and yen.
German government bonds firmed with British bonds or gilts, taking their cue from a rally in U.S. Treasury bonds overnight despite the expectation of a 0.25 percentage point rise in U.S. rates.
"A quarter-point rate rise is fully discounted now," said Norman Beauchamp, head of derivatives at the Cooperative Bank in London.

The market focus was firmly turned towards Washington where the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) was due to meet at 1400 GMT but not expected to announce the result of its deliberations until 1900 GMT -- well after European markets have closed.

With financial markets already primed for a quarter point rate increase by Fed policy-makers, analysts said investors were now looking at the prospects for continuing U.S. economic expansion, which has lasted six years.
As a result, the Dow Jones industrial average of blue chip shares, which was down 17 points as London markets closed on Monday, rebounded to close up 100.46 points or 1.48 percent.
Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan laid the groundwork last week for a possible rise by stressing the importance to the economy of keeping inflation down.

"If we allow that to get away, we will at the end of the day find that we have set in motion a set of forces which bring the long, sustainable, stable recovery to an end," the central bank chief told a Congressional committee.
However, until a decision emerges from the FOMC, one London dealer said he expected European markets to retain an element of caution.

Should the FOMC decide to raise rates by half a percentage point, share markets are likely to fall on both sides of the Atlantic. No rate increase could spark an initial, but short-lived rally, analysts said.
London blue chips, which had fallen 4.7 percent during the six sessions up until Monday, rebounded in early trading by more than one percent.

Among individual stocks, shares in Abbey National Plc rose 16.5p to 731 as bank stocks rallied from recent weakness and the market welcomed Abbey's failure to win control of insurer Scottish Amicable.

Analysts said there was relief that Abbey had not overpaid for the mutual insurer. Prudential Corp Plc, confirmed as the winning bidder, rose 17p to 556 after being seen deriving strategic and earnings benefits from the deal
Shares in British Steel Plc bucked the firmer market trend, sinking five pence to 156.5 after news that Germany's Krupp Stahl AG was calling off its takeover bid for Thyssen AG.
The shares of both German companies fell in Frankfurt trading, Krupp dropping 24 marks to 314.5, while Thyssen plunged 42 marks to 375.5.
The blue chip DAX-30 index was up 11.36 points at 3,333.2 by 1015 GMT.
French shares opened similarly higher, the CAC-40 index standing 17 points by mid-morning but down from its early highs.

Lyonnaise des Eaux and Cie de Suez remained strong on the back of an expected share swap bid of two Suez shares for one Lyonnaise share as part of a friendly merger. Lyonnaise was up1.74 percent at 584 and Suez added 0.43 percent to 278.5 francs.
On the foreign exchange market, the dollar started in Europe on a firm note before inching lower.
By 1015 GMT the currency was standing at 1.6857 marks and 123.42 yen compared with 1.6874 marks and 122.85 yen in late trading on Monday.
Since markets had already priced in a 25-basis-point hike in the U.S. Federal funds rate, there was little the dollar could do ahead of the meeting, analysts said.

"If the Fed doesn't spook the market with suggestions of a more aggressive-than-expected increase...if the Fed gives the indication it's not seeking to drive the economy back into recession, then the market can at least hold its present ground if not regain the highs of earlier this year," said Stephen Hannah, director of research at IBJ International here.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6857 marks and 123.42 yen, compared with 1.6874 marks and 122.85 yen in late trading on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 43.9 points, or 1.04 percent, at 4,258.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 17.67 points, or 0.69 percent, at 2,596.95.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 11.36 points, or 0.34 percent, at 3,333.2.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $350.90 an ounce versus $350.20 on Monday afternoon. Silver was four cents higher at $5.18.
